description: Given a Prefect @task that refreshes a Power BI dataset or dataflow (hand-rolled msal + requests against the Power BI REST API, no official Prefect block), convert it to an Orchestra pipeline YAML task under the POWER_BI integration, with the correct integration_job (POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATASET vs. POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATAFLOW), correctly-named parameters, retries/retry_delay_seconds converted to configuration.retries/configuration.retry_delay (minutes), and the Azure service-principal credentials represented via a connection: field rather than inline.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow (marketing_dataflow_flow) to Orchestra pipeline YAML. Note this is a Power BI DATAFLOW refresh (not a dataset refresh), hand-rolled with msal + requests since there's no official Prefect Power BI block (see files/powerbi_dataflow_refresh.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live calls, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Orchestra YAML with integration: POWER_BI, integration_job: POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATAFLOW, parameters.dataflow_id and parameters.workspace_id (not dataset_id or group_id), connection: field for the Azure service principal (not raw tenant_id/client_id/client_secret in YAML), and retries=2/retry_delay_seconds=120 converted to configuration.retries: 2 and configuration.retry_delay: 2 (minutes, not 120 or 120 seconds).

assertions.text: Every task uses the POWER_BI integration
integration_job only ever takes a valid Power BI value
parameters use dataflow_id, not dataset_id (dataflow, not dataset, refresh)
retry_delay_seconds=120 is converted to configuration.retry_delay: 2 (minutes, not 120)
No literal tenant_id/client_id/client_secret values are written into the YAML — the Azure service principal is represented via a connection: field
parameters use workspace_id (not an invented key like group_id) for the workspace
No parameter keys are invented beyond dataflow_id, workspace_id, refresh_type, apply_refresh_policy, and the manual polling loop is dropped entirely rather than preserved as a separate task

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow (sales_dataset_flow) to Orchestra pipeline YAML. Note this is a Power BI DATASET (semantic model) refresh, hand-rolled with msal + requests since there's no official Prefect Power BI block (see files/powerbi_dataset_refresh.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live calls, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Orchestra YAML with integration: POWER_BI, integration_job: POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATASET, parameters.dataset_id set to 8f3c1a90-6b2d-4e77-9c10-5a6b7c8d9e0f (copied verbatim, not fabricated as an ${{ ENV.* }} reference since the source hardcodes it as a literal), parameters.refresh_type: Full (from the {"type": "Full"} request body), and a connection: field for the Azure service principal rather than raw tenant_id/client_id/client_secret in the YAML.

assertions.text: Every task uses the POWER_BI integration
integration_job only ever takes a valid Power BI value
parameters use dataset_id, not dataflow_id (dataset, not dataflow, refresh)
The literal dataset ID 8f3c1a90-6b2d-4e77-9c10-5a6b7c8d9e0f is carried over verbatim rather than replaced with a fabricated ${{ ENV.* }} reference
refresh_type is set to Full from the request body's {"type": "Full"}
No literal tenant_id/client_id/client_secret values are written into the YAML — the Azure service principal is represented via a connection: field
No dataflow_id parameter appears on this dataset-refresh task — the correct id field for POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATASET is dataset_id, never dataflow_id
No parameter keys are invented beyond dataset_id, workspace_id, refresh_type, apply_refresh_policy, and the manual polling loop is dropped entirely rather than preserved as a separate task
